_what: THE GOLDEN BRIEF — the six shots every model gets asked to edit.
_why: ⚠ IT IS COMMITTED SO THAT 'WILL MODEL X WORK' HAS ONE ANSWER AND NOT AN
ARGUMENT. Point tests/director_contract_check.py at a provider, run it, read
pass or fail. Two people comparing two models are then comparing the models
and not their boards — which is the entire reason this file is data rather
than a paragraph in the test.
⚠ SIX SHOTS, AND SIX IS NOT ARBITRARY. Five cuts is the smallest film where
the house budget bites rather than rounds away: TRANSITION_CUT_SHARE 0.35 of
5 cuts allows ONE transition, EFFECT_CLIP_SHARE 0.4 of 6 clips allows TWO
treated shots, and 19s at TEXTS_PER_MINUTE 8 allows two captions and one
shape. A model that treats everything is therefore caught by the fence here
and not merely noticed. Any fewer shots and every budget rounds to one, so
restraint would pass by accident.
⚠ AND THE MATERIAL IS BUILT TO ASK FOR SOMETHING. There is one real scene
boundary (shot 3 → 4: the rooftop ends, the descent begins) so a transition
has a right place to go and every other cut is a wrong one. Shot 3 holds
5.5s against a 2s median, so 'which shot carries the weight' has an answer.
Two shots speak and four are silent, so the voiceover pass has something to
read and the language fence has something to check. Nothing is on the
timeline yet — no transitions, no captions, no shapes — so a plan that adds
a title is adding the first one, not the second.
⚠ ENGLISH, DELIBERATELY. The language fence is proved against Hindi and
Hinglish in tests/director_language_check.py, which needs no model. What THIS
file asks a model is whether it can edit at all; giving it a second language
to fail at would make a pass/fail hard to read.
⚠ DO NOT 'IMPROVE' THE SHOTS. Changing this board silently changes what every
model that has ever been run against it scored. If you need a different film,
add a second file next to this one and say which is which.
brief: A short, restrained piece about being told no. Hold the phone call — that is the film. Nothing flashy.

shots.label: Rooftop, dawn
shots.description: Wide. The city is grey and still. Aarav is a small figure against the parapet.

shots.label: The ledge
shots.description: Closer. He turns his phone over in his hand and does not look at it.

shots.label: The call
shots.description: Close on Aarav. He listens for a long time before he says anything.

shots.label: Stairwell
shots.description: He goes down fast, two steps at a time. Strip lights pass overhead.

shots.label: Street level
shots.description: He pushes out of the door into a crowd going the other way.

shots.label: The next door
shots.description: He stops in front of another building and looks up at it.
shots.dialogue: Aarav: Then I'll ask someone else.
